newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Mar palm oil output up 32 pct - Ivan Wong.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Mar palm oil output up 32 pct - Ivan Wong.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil output in March is estimated to have risen by 32 percent to 665,000 tonnes from February, crop forecaster Ivan Wong said on Monday.
This was slightly higher than his earlier estimate of 663,000 tonnes.

Wong put palm oil stocks at the end of March at 725,000 tonnes, unchanged from his earlier projection, compared with the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) 722,993 tonnes at end-February.
Wong, in his earlier report, estimated exports in March at 560,000 tonnes against February's 376,885 tonnes.
In his latest report, Wong said the output increase was largely accounted by Peninsular Malaysia where production rose 31 percent or 117,000 tonnes.
"The performance of major producers/millers ranged widely from up 20 percent to a staggering 86 percent," he said.
Stocks of crude palm oil are estimated to have risen 15,000 tonnes to 415,000 tonnes, with the entire increase accounted by East Malaysian states of Sabah and Sarawak.
Wong estimated stocks of palm kernel/palm kernel oil to have increased by 5,000 tonnes to about 140,000 tonnes, oil basis, at the end of March.
Malaysia palm oil supply-demand estimate/projection as of April 14, 1997. (All figures in '000 tonnes)
